technical_issues.issue: Inclination of 87.79° is prograde and cannot be sun-synchronous; it also contradicts the plotted ~97.8° at 600 km and the claimed retrograde orbit.
Semi-major axis 7171 km is wrong; 6371 km + 600 km = 6971 km.
RAAN 'initial value indicates the location of the launch facility' is incorrect; RAAN is set by the epoch and sun-synchronous condition, not the launch site.
Claims the true anomaly is undefined for a circular orbit. It is defined from the ascending node, with argument of latitude as the usual replacement for ω+ν.
States Kourou is at 45.05°N and 'very close to the equator'. Kourou is ~5.2°N; the latitude is wrong and the justification is inconsistent.
Proposes Vega E as the launch vehicle while acknowledging it is unbuilt, and the executive summary says 'direct launch' despite a piggyback plan.
Mean contact duration of 580.8 s is ~9.7 min, not 'almost twenty minutes'. The access table also repeats access number 13 and lists only 14 unique passes.
Claims a near-polar ground station maximises passes, but Mt Pleasant (~43°S) is not polar; pass frequency and number of stations are not quantified.
Uncontrolled re-entry from 600 km is not checked against decay time or the 25-year guideline. The 'graveyard' manoeuvre requires propulsion, which contradicts the 'without thrusters' statement.
Drag-sail sentence is truncated and unfinished.
Wikipedia is cited despite being explicitly unacceptable. Reference [10] is used for two unrelated claims, the entry is malformed, and citations [11]–[74] have no bibliography entries.

overall: Good STK-based effort with relevant screenshots and access data, but core orbital calculations contain errors, including a prograde inclination for a claimed sun-synchronous orbit and an incorrect semi-major axis. EOL is incomplete and the reference list is inconsistent and includes Wikipedia. Requirements are mostly addressed but several need more rigour.

feedback.summary: You have built a solid STK-based design for a single sun-synchronous satellite, with well-referenced rationale and useful access data. Core orbital calculations need correcting, including the inclination, semi-major axis and launch-site latitude. The end-of-life plan needs completing, and tidying the reference list will also strengthen your presentation.
next_steps: Recheck your orbital elements. A 600 km circular orbit has a semi-major axis of 6971 km, and a sun-synchronous orbit at this altitude is retrograde (about 97.8°). Make the COE table, text and plots consistent with each other.

Correct the Kourou latitude (about 5.2°N), the RAAN explanation (set by epoch and the sun-synchronous condition, not the launch site) and the mean contact duration (about 9.7 min). Quantify ground-station pass frequency and justify the number of stations.

Complete the end-of-life analysis: check decay time against the 25-year guideline, state whether the graveyard manoeuvre needs propulsion, and finish the drag-sail discussion. Replace Wikipedia with an acceptable source, fix the duplicated [10] entry and add bibliography entries for citations [11]–[74].

criteria.C1: Your primary mission, rationale for using one spacecraft and literature support are clearly argued, which earns an Adequate mark. To reach Accomplished, explicitly identify your operator and customers, which are currently only implied as marine and conservation scientists. Also resolve the conflict between the 'direct launch' wording in the executive summary and your piggyback launch plan.
criteria.C2: Your STK screenshots, access tables and orbit analysis give real evidence of design work. Errors undermine it: the 87.79° inclination is prograde, so it cannot be the retrograde sun-synchronous orbit you describe, and 6371 km plus 600 km is 6971 km, not 7171 km. Kourou's latitude is also misstated. To reach Accomplished, correct these, reconcile the contact duration with your table, and complete a decay and delta-V assessment for end of life.
criteria.C3: You reach conclusions on the main segments and sensibly flag the Vega E launch risk with a fallback. However, the conclusion mostly restates the report rather than drawing evidence-based conclusions on performance and end of life. Avoid overstating outcomes, such as claiming the mission prevents bleaching. To reach Accomplished, tie each conclusion to specific results from your analysis.
criteria.C4: Clear headings and a contents page give the report a sensible structure. Marks are held back by a broken reference entry, a duplicated [10] citation, citations up to [74] without list entries, Wikipedia use, a duplicated access number, a truncated sentence in the drag-sail discussion, and some tables lacking clear labels. Fix these and check that every in-text citation matches the reference list.
